sync.howTitle: How and when each type is sent
sync.how: Nothing is sent for a type that is off. Tracks: a changed bundle uploads once it has been left alone for ten minutes, so a running survey goes up once, after it stops and the corner labelling that follows it. Sessions: each lap as soon as it is saved, the session with its first lap; laps queue while the service is away. Live: one socket while the car is on track, a few frames a second, never a backlog. Everything retries with backoff and never blocks recording. A type the server switches off is turned off here too, and says so.
sync.disconnectBody: The stored token is forgotten and sync stops until a new token is saved. The token cannot be shown again — the service only reveals it once, when it is created.

cornerReport.col.brakeDelta.tip: Where the brake went on against the reference lap, in metres along the track. Negative = earlier, positive = later (deeper). Under 5 m is the same brake point.

cornerReport.col.zone.tip: Metres from the brake going on to its release.
cornerReport.col.slipPeak.tip: The most the car was rotated into the corner: degrees between where the nose pointed and where the car was going. More than the reference is more rotation — towards oversteer; less, or negative, is the nose pushing wide.
cornerReport.col.slipMean.tip: The same angle averaged from the corner's entry to its exit.
cornerReport.col.yaw.tip: How much the car rotated through the corner against how much its front wheels asked for (speed × wheel angle ÷ wheelbase). Under 1 is understeer, over 1 oversteer; compare it lap against lap after a setup change.
cornerReport.col.lock.tip: Metres of the corner the steering spent past full lock: the input kept rising and the front wheels could not turn further.
cornerReport.col.delta.tip: Time through this corner vs the reference lap. Positive = lost here.

channel.delta.title: Time diff (s)
channel.speed.title: Speed
channel.speed.description: How fast the car was going (km/h, or mph with imperial units). The dips are the corner minimums; a later, steeper drop is later braking.
channel.throttle.title: Throttle %
channel.throttle.description: The accelerator pedal as you pressed it, 0–100 %, before traction control acted on it.
channel.brake.title: Brake %
channel.brake.description: The brake pedal as you pressed it, 0–100 %, before ABS acted on it.
channel.coast.title: Coasting
channel.coast.description: On while neither pedal is above 1 % — time spent neither braking nor accelerating, which is usually time lost.
channel.gear.title: Gear
channel.gear.description: The gear engaged — compare where each lap shifted. Dashed: the gear GT7 suggested, where it suggested one. Shaded: a corner taken a gear above it.
channel.rpm.title: RPM
channel.rpm.description: Engine speed. A flat top is the rev limiter — a shift that came too late.
channel.boost.title: Boost (bar)
channel.boost.description: Turbo pressure above atmospheric, in bar; below zero is vacuum off the throttle. Flat on engines without a turbo.
channel.engineTorque.title: Engine torque
channel.engineTorque.description: The torque the engine was delivering, in GT7's normalized units (as decoded by the community): it follows the throttle and boost, dips below zero on the overrun and is 0 with the clutch in.
channel.yawRate.title: Yaw rate (rad/s)
channel.yawRate.description: How fast the car was rotating, either way, in radians per second. Beside Steering: plenty of lock with little rotation is understeer; rotation with little lock is oversteer.
channel.steer.title: Steering (rad)
channel.steer.description: Steering wheel angle as GT7 broadcasts it, in radians; left and right have opposite signs.
channel.wheelAngle.title: Front wheel angle (rad)
channel.wheelAngle.description: How far the front road wheels turned, in radians — what the tyres did with the Steering input. Where Steering keeps rising and this goes flat, the steering has run out of lock.
channel.racePos.title: Race position
channel.racePos.description: Your position in the race at each point of the lap — where places were won and lost.
channel.throttleF.title: Throttle applied %
channel.throttleF.description: The throttle after the driver aids acted on it. Where it sits below Throttle %, traction control was cutting power.
channel.brakeF.title: Brake applied %
channel.brakeF.description: The brake actually applied, after ABS acted on it. Where it sits below Brake %, ABS was releasing pressure. Live driving only: a replay doesn't carry it.
channel.tcsCut.title: TCS cut (% throttle)
channel.tcsCut.description: How much throttle traction control took away: Throttle % minus Throttle applied %.
channel.absRelease.title: ABS release (% brake)
channel.absRelease.description: How much brake pressure ABS gave back: Brake % minus Brake applied %. Live driving only, like Brake applied.
channel.accLat.title: Lateral g
channel.accLat.description: Sideways acceleration in g — the load of cornering. The traction circle uses a verified scale; this trace assumes the broadcast unit is m/s².
channel.accLong.title: Longitudinal g
channel.accLong.description: Acceleration along the car in g — braking and drive, with the sign GT7 broadcasts. The traction circle uses a verified scale and sign.
channel.accVert.title: Vertical g
channel.accVert.description: Vertical acceleration in g — kerbs, bumps and compressions. Nothing in a recording can verify its scale.
channel.bodySlip.title: Body slip (°)
channel.bodySlip.description: The angle between where the car points and where it is going. Positive is the nose to the right of travel: into a right-hander, out of a left-hander. Zero below 29 km/h.
channel.kinYaw.title: Kinematic yaw (rad/s)
channel.kinYaw.description: The rotation the front wheels asked for: speed × wheel angle ÷ wheelbase, the yaw rate with no tyre slip at all. Unsigned like Yaw rate, so the two lie side by side.
channel.yawBalance.title: Yaw balance (rad/s)
channel.yawBalance.description: Yaw rate minus Kinematic yaw. Below zero the car rotated less than its front wheels asked (understeer), above zero more (oversteer). Opposite lock reads nearer zero; Body slip shows it.
channel.tireSlip.title: Tire spd / car spd
channel.tireSlip.description: The wheels' average speed over the car's speed. 1 is rolling; above 1 is wheelspin, below 1 is locking.
channel.slipFront.title: Slip — front avg
channel.slipFront.description: Wheel speed over car speed for the front pair. Below 1 under braking is the fronts locking.
channel.slipRear.title: Slip — rear avg
channel.slipRear.description: Wheel speed over car speed for the rear pair. Above 1 on the throttle is wheelspin.
channel.slipFl.title: Slip — FL
channel.slipFl.description: Wheel speed over car speed for the front-left wheel: below 1 is locking, above 1 is spinning.
channel.slipFr.title: Slip — FR
channel.slipFr.description: Wheel speed over car speed for the front-right wheel: below 1 is locking, above 1 is spinning.
channel.slipRl.title: Slip — RL
channel.slipRl.description: Wheel speed over car speed for the rear-left wheel: below 1 is locking, above 1 is spinning.
channel.slipRr.title: Slip — RR
channel.slipRr.description: Wheel speed over car speed for the rear-right wheel: below 1 is locking, above 1 is spinning.
channel.ttFront.title: Tire temp — front avg (°C)
channel.ttFront.description: Surface temperature of the front tyres, averaged. Corner Detail treats 55–95 °C as the working window.
channel.ttRear.title: Tire temp — rear avg (°C)
channel.ttRear.description: Surface temperature of the rear tyres, averaged. Corner Detail treats 55–95 °C as the working window.
channel.ttBalance.title: Tire temp — F−R balance (°C)
channel.ttBalance.description: Front average minus rear average. Positive means the fronts run hotter — the car is working them harder, as it does when it understeers.
channel.bodyHeight.title: Ride height (mm)
channel.bodyHeight.description: How high the car sat, in mm. The dips are where it squatted under load or bottomed out.
channel.susFront.title: Susp travel — front avg (mm)
channel.susFront.description: How far the front suspension was compressed, averaged over both sides. Braking loads the fronts.
channel.susRear.title: Susp travel — rear avg (mm)
channel.susRear.description: How far the rear suspension was compressed, averaged over both sides. Acceleration loads the rears.

guide.title: Analysis guide
guide.footer: Every entry links to the {link} for the details.
guide.feature.choosingLaps.title: Choosing laps
guide.feature.choosingLaps.body: Click a lap chip to add or remove it; double-click one (or use the ref menu) to make it the reference everything is measured against — by default the session's quickest lap that counts. Add lap… brings in a lap from another session at the same circuit.
guide.feature.timeDiff.title: Time diff
guide.feature.timeDiff.body: The top chart: each lap's gap to the reference at each point of the track, in seconds. Positive is slower; where the line climbs is where time goes.
guide.feature.linedUp.title: Laps lined up by place
guide.feature.linedUp.body: Every lap is put on the reference lap's distance by where it was on track, so the charts compare the same point of a corner even when one lap took a wider line.
guide.feature.cursorZoom.title: Cursor and zoom
guide.feature.cursorZoom.body: Hover any chart, the map or the lap strip to move the cursor everywhere — charts, map, Corner Detail and traction circle. Drag across a chart, along the line on the map, or on the lap strip to zoom; drag the strip's edges to resize the window. ⌘/Ctrl + scroll on the map zooms about the pointer. Esc, a double-click or Full lap resets.
guide.feature.eventShading.title: Event shading
guide.feature.eventShading.body: Lockups shade Brake, wheelspin shades Throttle, bottoming and kerb strikes shade the suspension panels, and traction-control and ASM activity shade Throttle and Speed.
guide.feature.playback.title: Playback
guide.feature.playback.body: Plays the reference lap at 0.25–4× speed on the lap's own clock, so the cursor lingers in slow corners. The strip beside it shows steering, pedals, gear and speed.
guide.feature.raceLine.title: Race line
guide.feature.raceLine.body: The reference lap from above, coloured by the chosen lens: Inputs (green throttle, red brake, blue coasting), Speed, Gain / loss (where the compared lap gains and loses time), Tire temp (the hottest tire: cold, working, hot) or F−R temp (which axle's tires run hotter). The lens is remembered on this device and carried in the link. Other laps are drawn thin in their chart colours, brighter when zoomed in. Point at the line for every lap's time diff and chart values there (Hover readout in Layers).
guide.feature.sync.title: Sync: Time or Position
guide.feature.sync.body: Time draws each lap's car where it was after the same lap time as the reference, so a gap shows as distance on track. Position draws them level with the reference, where the charts compare them.
guide.feature.follow.title: Follow
guide.feature.follow.body: While playing, zooms the map in and pans with the reference car instead of framing the whole circuit.
guide.feature.layers.title: Layers
guide.feature.layers.body: The Layers menu switches each thing the map draws besides the reference line: the surveyed road, corner numbers, the other laps with their apex speeds and brake points, and the markers — speed peaks, kerbs, events (lockup ◆, wheelspin ●, bottoming ✚, kerb strike ✖) and TCS / ASM rings. Only layers the laps can fill are listed.
guide.feature.lapStrip.title: Lap strip and sectors
guide.feature.lapStrip.body: The bar under the map is the lap unrolled, coloured like the line, with the track's sectors above it and the corners below. S1…Sn zoom to a sector — the circuit's own when its boundaries are labelled on the Tracks page, thirds of the lap otherwise. A compact copy sits over the charts.
guide.feature.corners.title: Corners
guide.feature.corners.body: Numbers beside each corner on the map and under the strip — the circuit's labelled corners, or corners found on the reference lap. Click one, or press [ and ] to step through them, and everything zooms to it, from the braking zone to the exit.
guide.feature.fullScreen.title: Full screen and the surveyed road
guide.feature.fullScreen.body: ⤢ opens the map full screen, with scroll to zoom and drag to pan. On a surveyed circuit the road, its borders and walls are drawn under the lines; dashed amber marks stretches not surveyed yet.
guide.feature.cornerReport.title: Corner report card
guide.feature.cornerReport.body: Entry, minimum and exit speed and the time through each corner, in track order or — with the sort switch — biggest loss against the reference first. Click a row to zoom to that corner.
guide.feature.sectorTimes.title: Sector times
guide.feature.sectorTimes.body: Every lap of the session split at the track's sectors (thirds of the lap on a circuit without them), with the best of each sector and the best lap in purple. Laps that don't count toward bests are listed faint and hold no best.
guide.feature.braking.title: Braking points
guide.feature.braking.body: Brake Δ in the report card is where the brake went on against the reference: −14 is 14 m earlier. Beside it, the most pedal and the length of the braking zone. Hover a row to pin both laps' brake points on the map.
guide.feature.bodySlip.title: Balance: body slip per corner
guide.feature.bodySlip.body: Slip in the report card is how far the nose pointed into the corner past the car's direction of travel, in degrees. More than the reference is more rotation, towards oversteer; less is the nose pushing wide. Needs a recording with the body slip channel.
guide.feature.yawBalance.title: Balance: yaw against the front wheels
guide.feature.yawBalance.body: Yaw ÷ wheels in the report card is how much the car rotated through the corner over how much its front wheels asked for: under 1 is understeer, over 1 oversteer. Lock m is the metres spent past full steering lock. Needs packet C.
guide.feature.gearChoice.title: Gear choice
guide.feature.gearChoice.body: Dashed on the Gear panel: the gear GT7 suggested, where it suggested one. Shading marks the corners taken a gear higher — still above it at the slowest point — and the Tuning panel counts the reference lap's.
guide.feature.stintTrend.title: Stint trend
guide.feature.stintTrend.body: Lap time and tyre temperature for every lap of the session, split into stints at pit stops, with each stint's drift as a figure such as +0.18 s/lap. GT7 sends no tyre wear: temperature and pace drift are the only proxies.
guide.feature.gg.title: Traction circle (g-g)
guide.feature.gg.body: Lateral against longitudinal g for every moment of the lap — how much of the circle a lap uses is the reading. Needs packet B or wider; the footnote says whether the scale could be verified.
guide.feature.cornerDetail.title: Corner Detail
guide.feature.cornerDetail.body: The car from above at the cursor: tyre temperature as colour, suspension as bars, LOCK and SPIN badges. The small figures beside each wheel are the reference lap's.
guide.feature.gearing.title: Gearing
guide.feature.gearing.body: The focus lap's ratios, and the sawtooth: speed against rpm, a line per gear up to the redline, and the lap's own samples climbing each line to its shift. The lines are fitted to the lap; the reference is drawn in grey when its gearbox differs.
guide.feature.lapStatus.title: Partial, excluded, salvaged
guide.feature.lapStatus.body: Partial laps didn't time the whole circuit — a pit out-lap, or a race's lap 1 from the grid. Excluded laps were ruled out of bests by hand. Neither sets a best. Salvaged (⟲) laps were recovered from a stream that ended at the line, such as a replay.
guide.feature.sidePanels.title: Side panels
guide.feature.sidePanels.body: Race engineer notes for the session, the reference lap's tuning figures and class benchmark, fuel strategy, consistency across the best laps, and every lap's time against the session's median and spread.
guide.feature.sharing.title: Sharing a view
guide.feature.sharing.body: The address bar holds the session, laps, reference and chart channels, so a copied link opens this exact comparison.

tracks.check.sectorsNeedSurvey: Not configured. Survey this track before adding sector boundaries.
tracks.namedByUser: named by you from a lap
tracks.identifyTip: Match every unlabelled session against the surveyed circuits and name the ones that were driven on them. New sessions do this by themselves.
tracks.menu.importBundleHint: A track bundle JSON from another installation, merged by circuit name.
tracks.menu.uploadLogHint: Land a survey run's raw JSONL from another installation. It appears in the log list — assign it to a circuit to merge its evidence.
tracks.menu.pullSharedHint: Contributed bundles from the configured shared repo.
tracks.menu.sharedUnreadable: The shared repo could not be read.
tracks.menu.pullAllHint: Every circuit the shared repo offers, merged like single pulls. Safe to repeat — only what changed is added.
tracks.needs.title: Needs you
tracks.needs.count_one: {count} thing blocks auto-ID, sync or coaching
tracks.needs.count_other: {count} things block auto-ID, sync or coaching
tracks.empty: Nothing yet. Name a track from a lap in Sessions, or run a survey.
tracks.pullAllCircuits: Pull all circuits from the shared repo
tracks.mergeIntoTitle: Merge another bundle of this circuit into it — a friend's, or your own from another machine
tracks.renameTitle: Rename — and if the new name is another bundle, merge into it. Two spellings of one circuit are one circuit.
tracks.recheckTitle: Judge every lap driven here against the survey as it is now. This happens by itself after a survey stops or a bundle is merged, renamed or deleted; forcing it also says how many verdicts changed.
tracks.recheckNone: No sessions recorded here — nothing to re-check
tracks.logs.title: Survey logs ({n})
tracks.logs.blurb: Every run's raw JSONL — the complete, transportable record. Download one to move the run to another installation; it merges there by being assigned to a circuit, exactly like a local run.
tracks.footer.seeded_one: {count} shipped signature waiting for a circuit to be driven, listed here only once one has been
tracks.footer.seeded_other: {count} shipped signatures waiting for a circuit to be driven, listed here only once one has been
tracks.footer.installation: this installation is {source}, the id stamped on every vote it casts so merged bundles can tell whose evidence is whose.
tracks.footer.adminToken: Actions may need an admin token (Settings › Access).
tracks.shared.title: Shared bundles
tracks.shared.blurb: Contributed track bundles offered by the configured shared repo. Pulling one merges it through the same validation and voting path as an imported file, so evidence accumulates and your own corner labels are never overwritten.
tracks.shared.readError: The shared repo could not be read: {error}
tracks.shared.empty: The repo lists no bundles yet.
tracks.shared.correctionsTip: The repo keeps a corrections file for this circuit — areas kept off the map, borders drawn in. A pull brings it along and the map here is compiled the way the repo's is.
tracks.shared.pullMergeTitle: Merge the shared evidence into your bundle — both sides' observations survive
tracks.shared.pullTitle: Fetch this circuit's bundle and start from everyone else's survey work
tracks.delete.title: Delete the bundle for {name}?
tracks.delete.body: Every border point, finish crossing and corner label for this circuit is removed. The survey JSONL logs are untouched, so a run can be rebuilt from one.
tracks.rename.title: Rename {name}
tracks.rename.label: Renaming onto an existing bundle merges the two — which is the fix for one circuit living under two near-miss spellings.
tracks.assign.title: Assign this run to a track
tracks.assign.label: The log is replayed through the normal merge path, so the result is the same as having named the circuit while driving.
cornerEditor.mode.apex: Click the map for each corner, in track order. Name them as you go.
cornerEditor.mode.moveApex: Click where this corner's apex should be.
cornerEditor.mode.entry: Click where the corner starts — turn-in.
cornerEditor.mode.exit: Click where the corner ends — the exit.
cornerEditor.mode.sectorEnd: Click where this sector ends — the split line.
cornerEditor.splits.needTimes: Every sector needs a time, as the game showed it.
cornerEditor.splits.placed_one: {count} sector placed from L{lap} — last sector {last}. Save to keep them.
cornerEditor.splits.placed_other: {count} sectors placed from L{lap} — last sector {last}. Save to keep them.
cornerEditor.title: Corners — {track}
cornerEditor.turnCountTitle: The official catalog knows this layout's turn count; it is the only outside check on whether the labelling is finished
cornerEditor.mapHelp: Scroll to zoom, drag to pan. Pick a corner to edit it.
cornerEditor.empty: No corners yet. Hit {place} and click your way around the map, starting with the first corner after the start line.
cornerEditor.apexTitle: Click the map to move this corner's apex
cornerEditor.sectionsTitle: Named stretches of road — the straights, mostly. The lap analysis export times each one and finds the speed trap in it.
cornerEditor.sectorsTitle: Where each sector ends, in track order; the last runs to the start/finish line. GT7 broadcasts none, so the sector times in Analysis are read off these. Without them the lap is split into thirds.
cornerEditor.fromSplitsTitle: Place the boundaries from the sector times a race screen showed for one of your laps
cornerEditor.splits.blurb: Pick a lap at this circuit and type each sector's time as the race screen showed it. The last sector is not typed — it is what is left of the lap — and each boundary goes where that lap was at that moment.
cornerEditor.splits.noLaps: No recorded laps at this circuit yet.
cornerEditor.splits.lapAria: Lap the split times belong to
cornerEditor.splits.addSectorTitle: One more sector before the last
cornerEditor.splits.over: the sectors add up to {total}, past the {lap} lap
cornerEditor.sectorEndTitle: Click the map where this sector ends
cornerEditor.splits.errNone: Enter at least one sector time.
cornerEditor.splits.errNoPath: This lap has no recorded path to place the boundaries on.
cornerEditor.splits.errNoTime: This lap has no lap time.
cornerEditor.splits.errPast: The sectors add up to {at} at S{n}, which is past the lap time of {lap}. The last sector is not typed — it is what is left.
cornerEditor.splits.errNoPosition: No position recorded {at} into the lap.
tracks.why.nameExact: the name matches this layout exactly
tracks.why.lengthAgrees: {name}, and the measured lap length agrees ({length} m)
tracks.why.lengthDisagrees: {name}, but the measured lap length disagrees ({length} m)
